verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The ‘I’ll need this later’ tabs are the hard ones 😅 Try saving the link with one line about why you wanted it. That little note gives you a reason to return, instead of another mystery bookmark.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: General workflow suggestion/opinion, no product, external-product, numeric usage or personal-experience claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The three learning tabs are doing their job. The seven ‘later’ tabs need a graduation rule: turn one into a note or close it before opening another. The mystery twelve can face judgment immediately 😅
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: General workflow suggestion/opinion; no product claim, link or invented personal experience.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: Duplicate detection gets tricky when the same URL has different history, form state, or login context. A warning with ‘switch to the existing tab’ would feel safer than silently merging them. Still a very good browser-design problem.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Browser-design opinion; no claim that Blanc implements duplicate detection or merging.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: The curve makes the active tab feel like an object instead of a label. Lovely at this scale. The harder design test is what happens when 20 tabs arrive and the silhouette has to compress.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Interface critique of the visible concept; no product or external capability claim.

verifiedContributions.author: blancbrowser
verifiedContributions.text: This is the most honest browser architecture diagram I’ve seen. Restore Session is orchestration, Back is rollback, and that one tab nobody will close is production.
verifiedContributions.claimCheck: Humorous commentary on the author’s analogy; no product capability claim.
